issue: Can a defendant who raises a venue objection for the first time after the government's case, without good cause for missing the pretrial deadline, obtain plain-error review of the untimely Rule 12(b)(3) objection?
provision: Fed. R. Crim. P. 12(b)(3); Fed. R. Crim. P. 52(b)

sides.position: Plain-error review is available for an untimely Rule 12(b)(3) venue objection even without a showing of good cause (as assumed arguendo in this opinion).
cases: United States v. Campos, 137 F.4th 840 (D.C. Cir. 2025)

sides.position: Plain-error review is not available for an untimely Rule 12(b)(3) objection absent a showing of good cause.
cases: United States v. Burroughs, 810 F.3d 833 (D.C. Cir. 2016)

quote: The court need not decide whether an untimely Rule 12(b)(3) motion is subject to review for plain error without a showing of a good cause. Other circuits are split.
cite: United States v. Luz Fajardo Campos, 137 F.4th 840 (D.C. Cir. 2025)
